topic.title: Considerations during Thermal Solution Assembly and Disassembly

body.p: During the process of thermal solution assembly, disassembly, repair, and/or rework, various factors can result in a higher concentrated load, peak pressure, and non-uniform pressure distribution. This, in turn, can lead to increased die damage risk, such as backside die crack or backside die chipping.

Recommendations are provided in this section to help identify and avoid some of the main factors that contribute to the risk of die damage during thermal solution assembly, disassembly, repair, rework, and beyond. Always ensure proper care is taken to minimize die damage risk.

table.title: General Considerations on Die Loading and Pressure Uniformity1

entry.p:
Key factors influencing load magnitude and distribution are:
Loading center
TIM type
Excess warpage of cold plate
Misaligned TIM dispense from die areas
Assembly/disassembly screw sequence
Thermal solution tilting during assembly/disassembly
Board support during assembly/disassembly

row.entry: Avoid load concentration at die edge or corners during thermal solution assembly/disassembly and after assembly, which could increase risk of die crack.
An ideal load is distributed as uniformly as possible on the die(s) during and after thermal solution assembly/disassembly onto the Intel SoC package.

Avoid sliding or dynamic lateral movement of thermal solution on the die(s) during assembly/ disassembly. Avoid any relative movement between the board, backing plate and thermal solution during assembly/disassembly. This can lead to die damage.

entry.p: Ensure the peak pressure on the die(s) does not exceed the specified value in Maximum Pressure at any point during or after thermal solution assembly/disassembly.
Collect mechanical quality and reliability validation data to risk assess thermal Solution assembly process. Refer to the Intel Mobile SoC Die Loading Measurement Techniques, (#556532)

row.entry: Avoid foreign material (FM) deposited on the die(s) or thermal solution surfaces. This can cause concentrated loading on die(s) during thermal solution assembly/disassembly that can lead to die damage.

table.title: Thermal Attach Torque and Screw Sequence 1

ul.li: Ensure regular calibration of the screwdriver used for thermal solution assembly/disassembly.
Torque of 2.0 kgf-cm or less is recommended for assembly/disassembly process.
Ensure optimal screw sequence is used for thermal solution assembly/disassembly to minimize concentrated load during and after assembly process.

Every thermal solution design has its own optimum screw sequence that results in minimum concentrated loading during assembly/disassembly and after assembly. It is recommended to choose a screw sequence for each specific thermal solution and each Intel SoC package to reduce load concentration.
Unoptimized screw sequence can result in higher concentrated peak pressure on the die(s) during assembly/disassembly and after assembly, and can lead to die damage.
Refer to the Intel Mobile SoC Die Loading Measurement Techniques, (#556532), for a methodology to determine the optimized screw sequence.
An example is shown below of a specific 4-point thermal attach design, using two different torque sequences.
The respective impact on concentrated peak pressure is shown for each torque sequence.
In this example, Screw Sequence 1 is preferred over Screw sequence 2, since it results in a lower peak pressure on the die during thermal solution assembly/disassembly.
